review_notes: I read the whole file and checked poitouKernel in PoitouTransform.lean. I also searched Mathlib for existing sinh/cosh bounds and read Real.fourier_deriv. Most lemmas are already stated for general f, f', f'' (the derivative and kernel-bound lemmas) or are inherently about the regularized Tartar function. The one clear case of over-specialisation is the kernel bound for regularizedScaledTartar. The two Fourier-derivative lemmas are thin instances of Real.fourier_deriv, so I did not report them. I did not compile any proposed replacement.

findings.excerpt:
|poitouKernel (regularizedScaledTartar y δ) x| ≤
      Real.exp (-δ * x ^ 2) := by
  rw [poitouKernel, abs_div, abs_of_pos (Real.cosh_pos _)]
findings.problem: The proof uses only the fact that poitouKernel f x = f x / cosh (x/2) with cosh ≥ 1. It never uses any property of regularizedScaledTartar apart from the Gaussian bound on |f x|. The real content, |poitouKernel f x| ≤ |f x| for every f : ℝ → ℝ, is buried inside the Tartar-specific statement and re-derived with an awkward simpa/mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left step.
findings.proposed_change: Add a general lemma `theorem abs_poitouKernel_le (f : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : |poitouKernel f x| ≤ |f x|`. Proof: `rw [poitouKernel, abs_div, abs_of_pos (Real.cosh_pos _)]; exact div_le_self (abs_nonneg _) (Real.one_le_cosh _)`. Then restate the current lemma as `(abs_poitouKernel_le _ x).trans (abs_regularizedScaledTartar_le_gaussian y δ x)`. The same general lemma works for any other test function f with a pointwise bound, and the file's own derivative bounds (`abs_poitouKernelDerivative_le`, `abs_poitouKernelSecondDerivative_le`) are already stated for arbitrary f.
findings.benefit: The general inequality becomes reusable for other test functions, and the Tartar-specific lemma becomes a one-line corollary. Readers can see that the cosh factor only ever helps, and the awkward calc disappears. The degenerate case f x = 0 is covered, since div_le_self only needs 0 ≤ |f x| and 1 ≤ cosh.

evidence.excerpt:
noncomputable def poitouKernel (f : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  f x / Real.cosh (x / 2)
